title: Beautiful Katamari
subtitle: Roll up the world after another royal mistake
summary: Beautiful Katamari is Now Production's Xbox 360 action-puzzle game, first released in North America on 16 October 2007. body: Beautiful Katamari is Now Production's Xbox 360 action-puzzle game, first released in North America on 16 October 2007. A tennis serve from the King of All Cosmos tears open the universe, leaving the Prince to rebuild celestial bodies by gathering objects on Earth. The player rolls a sticky ball that collects anything small enough to attach. As it grows, the same surroundings offer progressively larger targets. The absurd story gives a simple physical activity another cosmic purpose, turning household clutter and city streets into material for repairing a mistake made far above the Prince's station.

An object that blocks a small katamari may become something to collect after a few more turns. Progress therefore changes how the player reads a familiar area. The best route at one size may no longer be useful once larger objects can be taken, encouraging a continuing reassessment of the surroundings. Rolling with two sticks gives the ball weight and direction, while awkward collections can make its movement less tidy. The pleasure comes from recognising that a space which first seemed enormous has gradually become another layer of things waiting to be gathered.

Jun Moriwaki directed the game, with music credited to Yoshihito Yano and Tetsuya Uchida. A planned PlayStation 3 edition was abandoned, making Beautiful Katamari an unusual Xbox-exclusive chapter in a series previously associated with PlayStation. Japan received it two days after North America, with Europe following in February 2008. Its central activity remains deliberately recognisable. New surroundings and a high-definition presentation give another setting to the change of scale that defines Katamari: the Prince starts by collecting small objects and ends by treating much of the landscape as part of the same ball.
